clips.text_en_b2: Putting aside the obvious question, Bitcoin versus gold over the next decade is genuinely tough to call. Bitcoin has historically delivered far higher returns, although gold offers stability that crypto simply cannot match. The /biz/ thread has already blown past 200 replies, with anons fiercely debating which asset would come out on top if you had to hold just one.
clips.text_en_c1: Imagine you were forced to hold a single asset for the coming decade, would your bet be on Bitcoin or gold? Someone posed that very question on /biz/ earlier this evening, and within a couple of hours the thread has already accumulated roughly two hundred replies, most of them degenerates arguing over which is the superior store of value. The case for gold rests on its historical stability and centuries-long track record as a hedge against inflation, whereas Bitcoin advocates counter that its asymmetric upside dwarfs any precious metal, particularly if institutional adoption continues along its current trajectory.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial question resurfaced on /biz/ tonight: presuming a ten-year holding horizon with no possibility of diversification, which asset class merits conviction — Bitcoin or gold? The thread has already metastasised past two hundred replies, each participant convinced that macroeconomic literacy resides exclusively on their side of the argument. Gold adherents extol its millennia-long scarcity and its immunity, or so they claim, to the caprice of regulatory whim, while the Bitcoin maximalists counter that no finite commodity has ever compounded at a comparable rate without surrendering eventually to obsolescence. The OP, meanwhile, confesses to bleeding capital through CFD positions and to having abandoned his licensing examinations mid-module, the syllabus itself now collateral damage. Invoking the wisdom of the congregation appears to be his last remaining strategy.

If it pumps, you ride the wave; if it flops like SNL 2.0, you cut your losses quickly. The /biz/ thread is buzzing tonight, although most anons are warning against going too heavy on a meme coin rally.
clips.text_en_c1: Dogecoin is being strapped to a goddamn rocket in three days, courtesy of an upcoming SpaceX mission, and you still cannot bring yourself to take a position. The thesis is straightforward: if the launch goes well and sentiment holds, the token should rally on sheer spectacle, whereas a botched mission would inevitably drag it back down to meme-coin purgatory. The sensible play, therefore, would be to ape a modest position ahead of liftoff and unwind before the inevitable SNL-style rugpull scenario plays out, unless of course the spectacle reignites the broader hype cycle entirely.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous poster on /biz/, evidently animated by the prospect of imminent Dogecoin-funded extraterrestrial exposure courtesy of an upcoming SpaceX mission scheduled within the seventy-two-hour window, has tendered his unsolicited counsel to the assembled masses: allocate a modest position, ride the speculative exuberance, and liquidate before the inevitable comedown transforms the episode into a second SNL debacle. Alternatively, should momentum persist, the resultant mania may inaugurate an entirely fresh cycle of retail FOMO. The thread, predictably, has bifurcated into true believers who consider five-figure Doge imminent and fatalists for whom the asset remains, as ever, a satirical instrument awaiting its terminal collapse. One trader has even opened a prop firm position he can ill afford to lose.

clips.topic_en: When to Cut After Lean Bulk
clips.text_zh: lean bulk完幾時cut走skinnyfat？2025年5月83kg肥佬，cut到2026年4月65kg廢到舉唔到20kg bar，之後lean bulk到而家80kg。3x8 bench 1 pl8，squat 3x6 90kg，deadlift 3x8 120kg。睇落有肉但唔知夠未。肥仔信今日又叫我去gym 🙄
clips.text_en_b1: How do i know when ive bulked enough to cut and escape skinnyfat. May 2025 i was 83kg fat, almost no muscle. Aggressive cut till mid april 2026, i was 65kg skinnyfat, trouble benching even the 20kg bar. Then i lean bulked up till now, back up to 80kg, benching 3x8 at 1 plate, squatting 3x6 90kg and deadlifting 3x8 120kg.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking when to cut after lean bulk
clips.text_en_b2: The trick is figuring out when to cut and finally escape skinnyfat territory after a long lean bulk. Back in May 2025, I was 83kg and carrying nothing but fat, so I went aggressive on a cut until April 2026, dropping to 65kg while barely handling a 20kg bar. After bulking back to 80kg, my lifts now sit at bench 3x8 at one plate, squat 3x6 90kg, and deadlift 3x8 120kg.
clips.text_en_c1: How on earth does one determine whether one has actually accumulated sufficient lean mass to warrant transitioning back into a cut and finally shedding the residual skinnyfat physique for good. In May 2025 I tipped the scales at a rather unflattering 83 kilograms, essentially adipose tissue with negligible muscle underneath, whereupon I embarked upon what can only be described as an aggressive deficit that persisted until roughly April 2026, at which point I had whittled myself down to a frankly emaciated 65 kilograms and could scarcely bench the empty 20 kilogram bar.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ regular has solicited the collective's diagnostic acumen regarding the optimal juncture at which to terminate a prolonged lean bulk and commence a cutting phase, having traversed an instructive gauntlet of body recomposition since May of 2025. His trajectory commenced at a corpulent eighty-three kilograms with negligible muscular substrate, descended via aggressive deficit to a dysmorphic sixty-five by April of 2026 — at which nadir he struggled to press even the unladen twenty-kilogram barbell — and has since clawed his way back to a credibly muscular eighty kilograms. Current lifts include a 3x8 bench at one plate, a 3x6 squat at ninety kilograms, and a 3x8 deadlift at one-hundred-twenty. He now inquires whether additional mass accrual is warranted before initiating the next caloric deficit.

clips.text_en_b2: Because it ticks nearly every box, this food has become a staple across both cutting and bulking phases. It delivers plenty of protein while letting you skip a few extra dishes, and as a bonus, it actively supports your gut microbiome. The /fit/ thread is full of anons swapping recipes, although plenty are stuck on deadlines and barely have time to cook anything at all.
clips.text_en_c1: This particular foodstuff resolves a frankly disproportionate number of nutritional headaches simultaneously, since it delivers a substantial quantity of high-quality protein that slots seamlessly into either a cutting or bulking protocol, functions as an unfussy staple capable of supplanting several more elaborate dishes, and, as if that were not sufficient, confers tangible benefits upon one's gut microbiome as a convenient bonus. The corresponding /fit/ thread devolves, predictably, into anons squabbling over which culinary workhorse actually merits the title, with no clear consensus emerging after several hundred posts.
clips.text_en_c2: A lengthy /fit/ discussion has crystallised around a single, ostensibly humble ingredient whose nutritional profile renders it indispensable across any macronutrient manipulation, whether the practitioner is running a caloric surplus or, conversely, an aggressive deficit. Anons enumerate its virtues with quasi-religious fervour: a complete amino acid distribution, unparalleled versatility permitting the substitution of multiple dishes from one's weekly meal plan, and, somewhat unexpectedly, prebiotic properties that nurture the gut microbiome — a benefit most lifters would previously have considered orthogonal to their goals. The thread has devolved into the customary sectarian bickering over preparation methodology, with several posters confessing that domestic cooking itself has become an unaffordable luxury given their professional obligations and the demands of pending examinations.

clips.text_en_b1: Dario Amodei says we need government regulation. Sam Altman says we need government regulation. Elon Musk says we need government regulation. I see what theyre doing here. Funny how they start screaming come regulate us right after opensource models are catching up.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread calling out AI CEOs' regulation push

signal.rationale: Commentary on AI industry politics, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Funny how Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk have all suddenly decided we desperately need government regulation. The pattern is pretty obvious: the moment open-source models start catching up, the frontier-lab CEOs start crying for regulators to come riding in. While they posture about saving humanity, /g/ anons are grinding through FE exams and quietly losing their minds.
clips.text_en_c1: It is, by any reasonable assessment, a remarkably conspicuous pattern when Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk all converge upon the same talking point within the same fortnight, namely that governments must intervene to regulate artificial intelligence before matters spiral catastrophically out of control. What renders this newfound enthusiasm for oversight particularly striking is the precise timing, since these entreaties to regulatory restraint have only materialised once open-source models have demonstrably begun closing the gap with their proprietary counterparts. Should the frontier laboratories succeed in having the development curve legislatively constrained, the competitive threat from open-source would be effectively neutralised, which would scarcely constitute a coincidence.
clips.text_en_c2: The synchronicity is, at this juncture, almost too pronounced to dismiss as happenstance: Dario Amodei clamours for governmental oversight, Sam Altman echoes the sentiment with polished sincerity, and Elon Musk — never one to forgo a regulatory moat — enthusiastically endorses the proposition. The pattern reveals itself with crystalline clarity to any observer conversant in the dialectics of Silicon Valley rent-seeking; frontier laboratories, having watched open-source alternatives narrow the capability gap with unsettling velocity, now discover an ardent appreciation for the licensing regimes they previously disdained. Whether this constitutes prudent stewardship of an emerging technology or a concerted campaign to ossify incumbent advantage under the guise of public safety remains, as ever, a matter of ideological orientation. The poster, meanwhile, prepares for his FE examination.

clips.text_zh: Dario slowing down、Musk on board、Altman tapping out，P(doom)得返1%。frontier model全部撞牆。transhumanist輸到喊。AI末日派正式贏咗，香港人睇住就好，繼續溫FE 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Dario slowing down, Musk on board, Altman tapping out. P(doom) status is now 1 percent. You fucking lost transhumanist trannies. The frontier models are slowing down. They are ready to deal with China. Total AI doomer victory, according to the /pol/ poster tonight.

signal.rationale: Geopolitical/AI narrative post, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: The doomers have effectively won, according to a celebratory /pol/ poster tonight. Dario is slowing down, Musk is on board, and Altman has tapped out, which has dragged P(doom) down to a mere one percent. With frontier models visibly hitting a wall, the transhumanists are eating crow, and the West is finally gearing up to deal with China rather than racing ahead.
clips.text_en_c1: The doomers have, by all reasonable metrics, prevailed. Dario has conspicuously decelerated his frontier-model deployment schedule, Musk has declared himself aligned with the precautionary camp, and Altman has effectively tapped out of the capability race altogether, with the prevailing P(doom) estimate collapsing to a scarcely credible one percent. The transhumanist faction, having so confidently bet upon exponential progress toward superintelligence, now finds itself consigned to the wreckage of failed predictions, weeping quietly into its rationalist blog archives. Crucially, the frontier models themselves appear to have hit a discernible plateau, their performance gains diminishing relative to the staggering computational expenditure required to elicit them.
clips.text_en_c2: A self-appointed oracle on /pol/ has declared the conflict effectively concluded, citing a confluence of capitulations that, in his estimation, constitutes irrevocable surrender by the transhumanist faction. The evidence, as assembled: Dario Amodei conspicuously decelerating his frontier deployments, Musk lending his institutional gravity to decelerationist talking points, and Altman, once the evangelist-in-chief of exponential progress, signalling quiet acquiescence. Aggregate P(doom), the poster notes with undisguised satisfaction, has compressed to a residual one percent — a figure that would have constituted wishful thinking mere months ago. The frontier models themselves, having encountered what appears to be a genuine capability plateau, are now deemed tractable enough for geopolitical accommodation with Beijing. Total victory, apparently, belongs to the doomers.

clips.text_en_c1: I have recently concluded a comprehensive rewatch of the Ghost in the Shell anime, and while the inaugural episodes left me somewhat underwhelmed, the series progressively revealed itself to be something quite extraordinary, with each successive instalment outdoing the last in both thematic ambition and atmospheric density. The question that now preoccupies the denizens of /a/, however, is when precisely the long-rumoured second season shall materialise, since the existing run remains frustratingly incomplete for those of us who have exhausted the supplementary material.
clips.text_en_c2: Having recently concluded his first proper engagement with the Stand Alone Complex canon, a /a/ contributor has registered his considered verdict: the inaugural episodes betrayed a certain narrative tentativeness, as though Oshii's singular directorial vision had not yet fully transmuted into the television idiom, yet the production accrued confidence with each successive instalment until what had begun as cautious curiosity hardened into genuine reverence. He now joins the perennial chorus demanding confirmation of a second season, a petition whose urgency intensifies with each passing fiscal quarter. The thread, populated by veterans conducting yet another rewatch, has devolved into affectionate litanies of favourite sequences and heated exchanges over the franchise's philosophical preoccupations. His own bandwidth, regrettably, is consumed by examination preparation.
